briefs.source_chain: Waller's dovish remarks (doubts a September hike, cites disinflation signs) cut hike odds to 51% from 63% and, alongside falling European gas prices, pause the global bond selloff and drive a cross-asset rally that favors equities over long-end bonds, therefore hawkish ISM services/prices-paid data partly offsets Waller without reversing the pricing move, therefore focus shifts to today's payrolls report (DB forecasts a +65k rebound) which will decide the Fed's path, while separately weak Japanese household spending sets up a BoJ meeting Bloomberg expects to be a 25bp hike.
briefs.brief_chain: Same chain: Waller's dovish comments cut hike odds to 51% from 63%, plus falling gas prices, pause the selloff and lift equities more than long bonds (with matching bps figures), hawkish ISM data offsets Waller, focus turns to today's payrolls print (DB's +65k forecast, steady 4.1% unemployment) after July's contraction, and Japan's spending contraction precedes a BoJ meeting reported to lean toward a 25bp hike.

distortions.what: Brief omits secondary data points — jobless claims (206k vs 205k expected) and the July trade deficit ($88.6bn vs $90.2bn expected).
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — these don't feature in the note's own causal framing of the day's move, which centers on Waller and the ISM print.

distortions.what: Brief drops Waller's specific hedging language (he'd consider a hike 'if inflation comes in hot').
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — the brief's own framing ('cast doubt on a hike') already conveys uncertainty rather than a firm no-hike call, consistent with the source's overall read that Waller 'won out' but wasn't unconditionally dovish.

briefs.source_chain: VIX term structure steepens (front end down since the Iran war, back end elevated) as SPX strings together a rare 23-day streak without a 1% decline, aided by the Citadel/Aschenbrenner deleveraging washing out crowded momentum positioning, therefore unlike the comparable 2024 streak — which had a dovish Fed hold and falling yields as a rates tailwind — today's streak lacks that support because yields are moving the other way, therefore the persistent long-dated VIX premium means volatility is being deferred rather than eliminated, setting up an eventual reckoning.
briefs.brief_chain: Same chain, same figures throughout (23 days, 90th percentile, -0.41 vs -0.47 correlation, ~75bp of cuts and ~40bp yield decline in the 2024 comp), same conclusion that volatility is deferred rather than eliminated.
